dialogues.speaker: Edler
dialogues.text: #Oh, if it isn't the Proto-Boss, {NICKNAME}! Miss Yelan said you'd be joining us for this operation...

dialogues.speaker: Edler
dialogues.text: Everything's in place and absolutely airtight — that "Dark Financier" and his last few minions might as well clean their necks and get ready to meet Madame Guillotine.

choices.text: You're back already? That was quick!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: All I have to do is help Miss Yelan distract a couple of bad guys. It's easy work and there are no tight deadlines to deal with.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Corder and Doddamani are tailing me pretty tightly. I spent a good few hours eating sweet treats with Hautemontagne and they had to stand there the whole time, pretending to be tourists perusing the tea!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I gave Hautemontagne a heads-up beforehand and told her to let the shopkeeper know to add a couple of zeroes to all the prices as a special offer for our hapless friends.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: In the end, they had to buy something, otherwise they'd have looked too suspicious. It was a real struggle for Hautemontagne and I to keep straight faces!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: It's a good way to help out the folks in Qiaoying Village by giving them a little extra income. Plus, I feel like I'm making amends for leading those criminals into their peaceful little hamlet.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I can't help feeling like I've brought them bad fortune. Maybe milking that bad fortune for money will replace it with an auspicious air?

choices.text: You're starting to sound more and more like a Liyue local...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Hehe, you can chalk that up to me doing my homework — and my incredible talent for tongues!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Back when we were fourth-grade deskmates, Hautemontagne used to say my impressions of our teacher were spot on! It's a skill that's been remarkably useful for my work...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: "When it comes to being a detective, it pays to be a cultural chameleon. Talk cute when chatting to kids, speak cultured when conversing with the Liyue elite..."

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: "And if you happen to find yourself rubbing shoulders with criminals, make sure you know how to swear like a sailor."

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's what Captain Grosrochard told me.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Though now that I think about it, I can't recall ever hearing him swear. Maybe when we're taking this lot in, I might get the chance to witness his sea legs at work. Or sea mouth, rather.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I'm looking forward to it!

choices.text: There's something familiar about your current way of speaking...
I'm not sure getting so excited over swearing is entirely healthy...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Don't worry, I won't be going around slinging profanities in front of any children. Whenever there are kids around, I talk like I'm reading a whimsical fairytale. And I certainly wouldn't say anything untoward when performing my official duties!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: You've gotta put on a menacing show when dealing with the worst of the worst. Otherwise, you'll soon find that they're the ones dealing with you!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: It's no skin off my back if criminals start calling me "executioner" or "guillotine." Though scary-sounding names like that are probably best left for heavy hitters like you.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Why don't you try throwing a few fierce words about?

choices.text: I—I guess I could try being a little more intimidating?

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's the spirit! Give 'em the ol' vocal evisceration!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: With your power and prestige, you wouldn't even need to be all that mean to leave the bad guys trembling.

choices.text: I need to be polite, or else I might lead Paimon astray...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: *sigh* Fair point. All of my colleagues keep saying how smart and sweet your little companion is. It wouldn't be right to be a bad influence on her.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: In which case... you can be fierce in secret, when Paimon isn't looking or listening!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Indeed. This operation's been going on for months now, and Miss Yelan's actions have been quick and decisive. I've never seen someone work with such efficiency!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Right now, only the Dark Financier's closest confidants remain free, and his operations have been scaled back immensely. It's only a matter of time before he's caught in our net...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: You don't think we're catching too few criminals to be worth your time, do you?

choices.text: Not at all. One big fish is worth a hundred tiny minnows.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's great to hear! If you want to help out in the future, I'll make sure to pick only the most difficult cases for you to crack. The hard ones are always the most fun!

choices.text: Well, a little. I do have a quota to fulfill.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I'm sorry to hear that! If you want to help out in the future, I'll make sure to let you know as early as possible. That way, there'll be more low-level grunts for you to round up!

choices.text: Actually, I'd like to learn more about these perps we're after.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: You're looking for the lowdown on the Dark Financier's gang? What exactly do you want to know?

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Of course. I'm sure Miss Yelan's already explained the basic hustle to you — they purchase items at auction with artificially inflated valuations and then, after enough such trades, the dirty Mora becomes impossible to trace.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Besides just exploiting the auction rules that allow buyers and sellers to remain anonymous, they have a whole bunch of other tricks to cover their tracks.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: For example, the Mora used to buy foreign valuables changes hands many times beforehand, even being used to buy other goods, which are then traded back for Mora elsewhere. They do this to escape surveillance.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Then, when they buy things abroad, they either use false personas or pay other people to make the purchases for them, which makes them virtually impossible to track through the stores' ledgers.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: On top of that, the "valuables" they sell at auction are actually just regular items. The sort of thing that's difficult to identify and track and then intercept in transit. Even if we do hunt one down, it usually doesn't help our case against the gang.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Just thinking about it is enough to make you want to scream, am I right?

choices.text: Yeah... I can feel my blood beginning to boil!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: And the Dark Financier has other ways of laundering money. Fake charitable foundations, film investments, shell corporations, the list goes on...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: He's been aggressively swallowing up the competition and acquiring their tricks and techniques in the process.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: But right now, things are in our favor.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Thanks to the help of the Spina di Rosula, we've managed to dismantle his network of dirty tricks and put a stop to most of his operations in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: As for this racket with the auction houses, it's already largely under our control — we've left a few loopholes open, but only so we can monitor who's using them.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: With your help, it's only a matter of time until we strike a decisive blow and take out the Dark Financier once and for all!

choices.text: Only a little. I'd like to give them a standard-issue beating.
How will you deal with the criminals?

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: I'm glad you asked!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: This matter concerns both Fontaine and Liyue. Besides the Dark Financier and his multiple layers of underlings, there are many people who have been unwittingly sucked into these crimes.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Following discussions between both nations, the current agreed-upon plan is for Liyue to round up and process all of the criminals within its territory, interview the suspects, and take statements in preparation for building a case.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: After which, Fontaine will arrange for the extradition of all related Fontainian subjects, whose assets will be thoroughly investigated to make sure that no guilty parties escape justice.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Once the Dark Financier is in custody, both nations will reconvene discussions to establish a joint body to prosecute all the criminals that have been caught.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Based on my experience, I imagine anyone who was paid to buy goods is going to have to forfeit whatever money they made and undergo some sort of correctional course — provided they didn't know they were aiding and abetting a criminal organization, that is...

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: For members of the organization themselves, those at the third-tier and above are facing a minimum of ten years behind bars.

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: Whereas the Dark Financier himself can expect to live out the rest of his days in a jail cell.

choices.text: Let's make sure we solve this case!

response.speaker: Edler
response.text: That's the spirit! I look forward to watching you work.
